Thanks for sending the initial DPA — attached is our round-1 redline (see attached 'DPA_Redline_v1.docx'). A couple of things we want to call out up front so we can move quickly:

- Subprocessor carveout: our legal team has requested an explicit carveout for LogiXData (analytics vendor) on pages 6–7. They want the option to prohibit that subprocessor for regulated datasets. - EU transfers: prefer an EU-specific addendum or SCCs rather than a generic transfer clause. Please confirm the mechanism Redwood proposes for transfers out of the EEA (SCCs + EU-US Addendum or alternate).
- Evidence: we need SOC 2 Type II and a current subprocessor inventory listing LogiXData and any cache/CDN providers.
- Execution: is DocuSign fine? Our procurement sometimes requires AdobeSign — happy to accept either, but we need to understand the preferred path and signer details.

On LogiXData specifically: we prefer to avoid bespoke carveouts that create asymmetric rights, but we can agree to either (a) list LogiXData as a named subprocessor with contractual flowdowns and evidence, or (b) accept a temporary customer-specific restriction for regulated data classes if NovaFin provides a shortform scope definition. I want to loop in Rishi (legal) to propose exact language.

DocuSign is our default and fastest path, but we can do AdobeSign where required — we'll flag that in the execution plan. Proposed next steps:
- Rishi will provide proposed responses to each redline by end of day.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 7 Oct 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA redline + subproc carveout question — counsel notes

Team — quick legal read and suggested positions for the customer redlines: 

1) Subprocessor carveouts: do not accept a permanent one-off carveout that exempts Redwood from flowdown obligations. Counterproposal: add a Customer-Specific Restriction section (new paragraph) that permits NovaFin to request restriction of a named subprocessor for a defined dataset where (i) NovaFin provides a narrow scope of data types and (ii) Redwood will attempt to re-route or replace the subprocessor within 30 days. If replacement isn't possible, allow a temporary suspension of processing for the affected dataset.

2) Notice & cure: propose 30-day notice and cure period for subprocessor concerns (Redwood to provide mitigation plan). Customer had asked for immediate prohibition; that creates operational and security risk.

3) Transfers: accept SCCs + EU Addendum. Do not accept language that makes Redwood the sole guarantor for third-party onward transfers; instead require contractual flowdowns and a right to audit process.

4) Liability: push back on unlimited liability tied to transfer clauses; propose caps consistent with commercial terms (we can flag this to Sales for negotiation).

5) Evidence: we will provide SOC 2 Type II and per-subprocessor attestations for critical providers (LogiXData included) — attach inventory PDF.

I'll prepare a redline with proposed language (tracked changes) and highlight negotiation buckets (subproc carveout, notice period, liability).

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: DPA redline + subproc carveout question — Redwood positions and execution plan

Emma — following up with Redwood's positions (see summary below) and an execution proposal. I pasted Rishi's counsel notes into the redline and attached a short DocuSign execution plan.

Summary of Redwood positions (high level):
- LogiXData: we will list it as a named subprocessor and provide contractual flowdown plus evidence (SOC2/attestation). If NovaFin requires a temporary restriction we can accept a scoped suspension for narrowly-defined regulated datasets while we attempt replacement.
- Notice & cure: 30-day notice and mitigation period (Redwood will provide plan).
- Transfers: SCCs + EU Addendum — we'll supply the addendum text; not acceptable to shift unlimited obligations for third-party onward transfers.
- Liability: we will not accept uncapped liability for transfer mechanics; propose to keep to negotiated commercial cap.

Execution: DocuSign preferred. Attached 'DocuSign_Proposal.pdf' shows: signer (NovaFin — VP Procurement or delegated signee), Redwood signee (Head of Commercial Ops), proposed signing order, and timeline to sign by 10/12. If NovaFin must use AdobeSign, we can accommodate but it will add 1 business day for setup.

If this approach is acceptable, I'll update the redline and upload into DocuSign for your review. Would you prefer we (a) send a DocuSign envelope with our proposed redline, or (b) upload your redline and route for signature?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute call Monday.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
